A task board your profiles work through, in the menu. With a server it runs there. On the built-in Linux it runs on the phone: a check every minute and a Hermes process per task, so it is heavy, and switching it restarts Hermes.

Hermes runs inside the Termux app in this mode. Install Termux from F-Droid (not the Play Store version), open it once, then come back and check again.
Hermes runs on your own server; this app connects to it over your private Tailscale network. No hosted server is provided.

Hermes stays on 127.0.0.1 and no port is opened to the internet: only your own Tailscale devices reach it, over an encrypted connection. Tip: turn on Device approval in Tailscale so every new device needs your OK.

“%1$s” is named like a photo or document, but it is really a program. Files like this are made to trick people, so it can\'t leave Hermes.

It installs Tailscale if needed and prints a sign-in link: log in with the account you use in this app. If Tailscale asks to turn on HTTPS, open that link too. At the end it prints your Hermes username and password.
